parts.prompt:
Which general property pair makes a metal useful for electrical wiring?
A. High density and scratch resistance
B. Thermal conduction and material brittleness
C. Low density and electrical insulation
D. Electrical conductivity and material ductility

D. Electrical conductivity and material ductility. A wire must carry current and be drawn into shape.
Distractor explanations: A: Neither density nor scratch resistance establishes current conduction and drawability. B: Brittleness is unsuitable for drawing wires; thermal conduction is not the required electrical property. C: Electrical insulation prevents the wire from carrying current.
marking_guidance: Correct option D (1). D. Electrical conductivity and material ductility. A wire must carry current and be drawn into shape. Distractor explanations: A: Neither density nor scratch resistance establishes current conduction and drawability. B: Brittleness is unsuitable for drawing wires; thermal conduction is not the required electrical property. C: Electrical insulation prevents the wire from carrying current. No mark for more than one selected option.

parts.content_target: Compare metal reactivity using a controlled acid reaction, measurements and a defensible conclusion. Plan an investigation with predictions, suitable apparatus and techniques.
parts.credit_requirement: Plan metal/acid comparison: same acid concentration (1), same acid volume/temperature (1), matched exposed metal area (1), collect evolved gas safely (1), measure volume against time (1), compare rate to infer relative reactivity (1).
parts.prompt: Plan a teacher-supervised comparison of magnesium and zinc reacting with excess dilute hydrochloric acid to investigate relative reactivity. Include controls, gas measurements and the comparison used for a conclusion. No flames are permitted near the hydrogen-generating apparatus.
parts.canonical_answer: Use the same dilute HCl concentration, volume and temperature in separate comparable flasks. Match exposed strip areas and clean surfaces consistently. Collect hydrogen through a leak-free delivery tube into a freely moving gas syringe, starting timing at mixing. Record gas volume at equal time intervals and repeat each metal. Compare early gradients or average volume change per equal interval; a larger rate supports greater reactivity under these controlled conditions. Keep acid in excess and hydrogen away from flames; do not test sodium or potassium with acid.
marking_guidance: Same acid concentration (1).
Same acid volume and temperature (1).
Matched exposed metal area (1).
Safe workable gas collection (1).
Gas volume measured against time (1).
Compare rates to support relative-reactivity conclusion (1). Accept equivalent controlled safe collection; maximum six marks.
